ClientResponses.Response:
Your feedback is very important to us. We are very sorry to hear you are seeing signs of rust on your grill. We are here to help. 

If your grill is located in a coastal or humid area, or if chlorine is present in your environment, additional maintenance will be needed to keep up the appearance of the exterior steel parts.
 
At the first sign of staining/discoloration/surface rust we would recommend cleaning with stainless steel cleaner (ex. Bar Keepers Friend). Once cleaned, we recommend using a stainless steel polish (ex. Weber's brand) to keep it looking its best in-between cleanings.
 
Once a week we would recommend wiping down the grill with a wet towel or rag and then drying completely.
 
We would only recommend covering your grill if you know inclement weather is coming.
 
The quicker you get at a stain the easier it will be to clean off.

Our Care team will reach out to assist you further. Please look for an outreach email from us soon. Thank you!

Results.ReviewText:
This is my fifth weber since 1984. I have owned a full-sized kettle, a Smokey Joe, a 2004 propane 2-burner, open cart Spirit (which I just replaced with the E-310). and a charcoal 22" Weber perform cart/kettle. What I can say about those four is that they were rock-solid. Nineteen years for the Spirit with only one failure - the igniter which went almost immediately. I replaced the cast iron grates and flavorizer bars once in those 19 years. No rust on the cooking box or lid; minor surface rust on a few areas on the legs. A spray paint with Rustoleum every three years and it looks new. It cooked very well right up until the last night I used it. I wish I could get the exact replacement.

The new E-310. 
Well maybe if I had never owned the 2004 Spirit I would be more satisfied. If I had to use one word to capture the difference in the two, it would be flimsy. 

The old unit was an indestructible beast. On the E-310 the thickness and weight of the cooking box and lid is a fraction of what it was. The grates and flavorizer bars are thinner and lighter. The burners and burner connecters are lightweight and move!  All the parts under the grates shake and rattle during normal cooking procedures. The stainless-steel side burners aren't completely stable (and they are not fold-downs). My neighbor next door has the cart version of the 310 and one of his side tables is permanently bent down. My previous Spirit side table was a composite material with a fold-up extension. Rock soild; you could pick up the grill holding onto it without a wobble. I wouldn't dare try that with the E-310.

And I don't get the fascination with stainless steel. It is thin and difficult to maintain in the long-term. I've had the unit for six weeks and there are already discolorations - and I use stainless steel cleaner wipes.

The metal base cabinet is lightweight.  Minimal force can bend the door. The magnet is not powerful enough to properly seal the doorWhere the supports meet the base, water tends to accumulate - a breeding ground for rust.

Now' after the first three uses they were fully seasoned - perfectly well. Steaks and burger have cooked very well. The burners spring to life using the igniter and spread instantly when burners 2 and 3 are activated. This is far superior than my previous Spirit. The unit reaches full heat very rapidly and cooks very well with just two burners if that is all the area I need. 

So, I can honestly say it is working fine. And frankly, I had read reviews that shared my concerns but I considered it the best of what is currently available. I'm just wondering what cutbacks in materials will mean in the long term.

Would I buy this model again compared to other brands in the same category? Probably would.
Results.Title: Good, but not like the old days.
